title: Generate landscapes with different spatial patterns
text: quickest way generate training data create_landscapes(). generates multiple landscapes balanced across available patterns. landscapes returned list landscape objects (see info data structure). can visualized using plot_landscape_list() function:  default, landscapes created balanced way, pattern type represented equally generated set. Specific patterns can selected create subset patterns using patterns argument. example, create landscapes labyrinth, spots, clustered patterns:  modify size (number pixels x- y-direction) generated landscapes, use ncol nrow arguments. default, landscapes created size 100x100 pixels.  default, landscapes rotated angles randomly chosen 0 360 degrees. ensures classifiers trained landscapes invariant landscape orientation. can disable random rotation setting add_rotation parameter FALSE. can also control used rotation angles directly using rotation_angles.  can modify default parameters generated landscapes specific pattern passing list parameter values params_list argument. example, create landscapes spots larger size:  check parameter names default values pattern type, see function help create_landscape().
code: # Create 20 landscapes balanced across all pattern types landscapes <- create_landscapes(n = 20) #> ✔ Successfully generated all 20 training landscapes # Plot all landscapes plot_landscape_list(landscapes) # Check how many landscapes of each type were generated table(purrr::map_chr(landscapes, ~ .x$pattern)) #>  #>     bands      bare clustered     dense   diffuse   fingers      gaps labyrinth  #>         2         2         2         2         2         2         1         1  #>    random     sharp     spots  #>         2         2         2 # Generate only specific patterns landscapes <- create_landscapes(   n = 12,   patterns = c("labyrinth", "spots", "clustered") ) #> ✔ Successfully generated all 12 training landscapes  plot_landscape_list(landscapes) non_square <- create_landscapes(   n = 3,   width = 50,   height = 20 ) #> ✔ Successfully generated all 3 training landscapes # Plot landscapes with custom size plot_landscape_list(non_square) no_rotation <- create_landscapes(   n = 3,   patterns = c("clustered", "sharp", "bands"),   add_rotation = FALSE )  defined_angles <- create_landscapes(   n = 3,   patterns = "clustered",   rotation_angles = c(45, 90) )  plot_landscape_list(c(no_rotation, defined_angles)) # Custom parameters for spot patterns pattern_params <- list(   spots = list(     n_spots = 15,     spot_radius = 10,     spot_radius_sd = 3   ) ) bigger_spots <- create_landscapes(   n = 12,   patterns = "spots",   params_list = pattern_params )  plot_landscape_list(bigger_spots)
